cands.name: Rodney Sadler
cands.bio: Rev. Dr. Rodney Sadler is a Baptist minister and Bible scholar from Charlotte. He holds degrees from Howard University (BA 1989, divinity 1992) and Duke University (PhD 2001). He won the Democratic primary over incumbent Carla Cunningham and was elected to NC House District 106 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Gov. Josh Stein, State Sen. Caleb Theodros, State Rep. Julia Greenfield and former Charlotte Mayor Jennifer Roberts (all Democrats).

Black Political Caucus of Charlotte-Mecklenburg, North Carolina Association of Educators, SEIU Local 32BJ, Sierra Club North Carolina, Sunrise Movement, Planned Parenthood Votes! South Atlantic, and the Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Sadler was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. He has held no prior elected office that we could find, so there is no legislative record to report. We found no independent news coverage of him. We found no documented stances on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, abortion, or police pay and pensions. His 2013 arrest at the General Assembly comes only from his own campaign site, and we found no news report or court record of it.

qual.background: Career pastor and Bible scholar with a Duke PhD. He has been an activist, including in the Poor People's Campaign. The pages show no prior elected office and no legislative, policy or budget career.

second-amendment.evidence: Criticizes legislators' laws that 'put more guns in our communities – and even in our schools,' saying they make people less safe.

workers-first.evidence: Criticizes laws that force local law enforcement to collaborate with the Trump administration on immigration and says he will defend immigrant neighbors; he also says blaming immigrants is a tactic of the wealthy.
